title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tan\beta$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
abstract: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tan\beta$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tan\beta$, $1\le \tan\beta \le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$. The lineshapes in the four search channels are governed by a simple complex parameter $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant to non-resonant amplitudes at the peak. Because the $H$ and $A$ bosons couple weakly to the considered final states, while being broadened by their decays to top quarks, $|\kappa|$ drops to values of a few for masses of $0.5$--$1$ TeV, even though the total widths remain at the percent level. The interference then increases the signal rates by up to tens of per cent, and distorts their lineshapes. For the present ATLAS (and presumably CMS) Run II exclusion limits, the net effect is nevertheless rather modest, except at the high-mass end of the $H\to hh$ contour, but it becomes important for the masses that will be probed at the high-luminosity LHC.

title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
abstract: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

title: A pseudoscalar Higgs boson interfering with toponium: a QCD analysis of $\mathbf{gg\to A\to t\bar t}$ near threshold
abstract: The CMS and ATLAS collaborations have observed an excess of $t\bar t$ events near threshold that is consistent with the formation of the pseudoscalar toponium state $\eta_t$. A pseudoscalar Higgs boson $A$ with a large coupling to top quarks could contribute part of this excess and the presence of the $A$ boson could be concealed. We point out that, if such a state exists with $M_A$ close to $2m_t$, it necessarily interferes with toponium, since both live in the colour--singlet ${}^1S_0$ channel and share the same Coulomb final--state interaction. Using exact leading--order amplitudes, whose relative phase is fixed by unitarity, and Coulomb resummation applied coherently to the QCD background, the $A$ boson signal and their interference, we show that the line shape is controlled by a single complex number $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant and non--resonant amplitudes at the peak. Unitarity fixes ${\rm Im}\,\kappa=-1$ exactly when $A$ decays into top quarks, so that the interference reduces the resonant rate by $2/|\kappa|^2$ and produces an exact zero of the ${}^1S_0$ amplitude just above $M_A$. The parameter $\kappa$ does not depend on the $A$ coupling to top quarks and, with the Coulomb--enhanced width we find $|\kappa|\approx1.5$--$1.7$ for $M_A=350$--$380$ GeV and, hence, the $A$ resonance is completely distorted. For an $A$ boson accounting for 50\% (25\%) of the observed excess, it enhances the toponium peak by about 10 to 70\% (5 to 35\%), and the threshold excess differs strongly from the sum of the toponium and $A$ contributions.

title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
abstract: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these "sealed worlds", we are able to test the accuracy and robustness of the workflows. We demonstrate the approach on four tasks built from CMS open data and present it as a way to reliably benchmark scientific work in experimental high-energy physics. At the time of writing, the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, reaches 60% of the score of the expert reference analyses on average, ahead of GPT 6 Astra at 38% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 31%. In individual sessions on one of the tasks, Gemini 4 Argon exceeds the reference. The benchmark is hosted at https://hep-ex-bench.github.io

title: In-in formalism & $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-product: no contribution from total time derivatives
abstract: In the in-in formalism, total time derivatives are sometimes argued to contribute nontrivially to inflationary correlators at the evaluation point, i.e., at the end of inflation. In this paper, we disprove this claim based on the path integral. After formulating the canonical quantization and the regulated path integral of systems with total time derivatives, we derive the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the correct operator ordering on the closed time path. In the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the evaluation point, or the turning point of the in-in contour, is merely an intermediate point and is never an endpoint of the generalized path integral contour. As a result, any apparent boundary contributions at the turning point of the forward and backward branches completely cancel out. We demonstrate this cancellation by re-analyzing examples in the literature, with an emphasis on contact terms associated with the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering overlooked previously.

title: Machine learning for trigger, reconstruction and generation
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly embedded in every stage of the LHC data-processing chain, from event generation to final reconstruction. This contribution reviews the latest ML developments from the ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations that were made public in the year preceding LHCP2026, following the workflow of the experiments: event generation and detector simulation, real-time trigger selection, and online/offline reconstruction. Highlights include generative models that accelerate the simulation of specific ALICE detector components by up to six orders of magnitude, the CMS AXOL1TL and ATLAS GELATO unsupervised anomaly- detection triggers now operating in Run 3, a quantised Deep Sets jet tagger for the CMS Phase-2 Level-1 trigger, ML-based jet energy correction and flavour tagging at LHCb, the first empirical scaling laws for transformer-based flavour taggers in ATLAS, and several transformer and graph- based reconstruction algorithms (ATLAS GN3 flavour tagging and MaskFormer tracking, LHCb GarNet, CMS MLPF) developed for HL-LHC operation.

title: Massless neutrinos in a left-right symmetric universe
abstract: This comment is a comment stimulated by the 1957 Goldhaber et al. experiment, that detected a massless left-handed electron neutrino with negative helicity. The standard description of this neutrino is by means of a Weyl spinor. It is shown below that this description is incomplete, and in fact one needs a massless Dirac spinor to comply with the requirements of quantum field theory. A Dirac spinor is composed of two Weyl spinors. This in turn raises the necessity to explain the fate of the right-handed electron neutrino, partner of the Goldhaber et al. experiment's one. A possible explanation for its invisibility is suggested here in terms of a left-right symmetric extension of the standard model.

title: Flavor Alignment and Operator Sensitivity in a Left--Right Universal-Seesaw Model
abstract: We analyse the flavour structure and low-energy operator sensitivity of a parity-related doublet universal-seesaw model with an imposed lepton triality. Degenerate bare singlet masses permit a basis in which light-light tree neutral flavour transitions vanish; the physical heavy masses remain nondegenerate. We connect this alignment property to the axial and scalar differences measured by $B_{d,s}^0\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and reproduce the six-state charged-vector mixing amplitudes for five reference masses. The reference analysis identifies kaon CP violation as the more sensitive flavour probe. Historical kaon data disfavour the lower reference masses, while estimates suggest that dimuon and radiative $B$-decay effects are harder to resolve at present precision. These comparisons use the specified reference spectrum and historical inputs. We also compare charged and neutral resonance rates with published search benchmarks. The vacuum hierarchy entails a cancellation of about $5\times10^{-6}$ at $M_{W_R}=80\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The initially thermal Dirac-neutrino branch has a dataset-dependent extra-radiation tension, strengthened in an illustrative mass-dependent decoupling estimate. For dimuon decays we establish operator selection rules and sensitivity estimates. The numerical flavour results cover meson mixing and charged-vector dipoles. We give no dimuon branching-fraction prediction or global allowed region.

title: Superdaisy Resummation in Theories with Broken Gauge Symmetries
abstract: We extend the partial dressing resummation scheme for the finite-temperature effective potential to the gauge and ghost sectors of spontaneously broken gauge theories and apply the resulting framework to the Standard Model. Going beyond the usual high-temperature treatment, we retain the full mass dependence of the thermal self-energies and determine the scalar, gauge-boson and ghost masses self-consistently from a coupled system of gap equations. The solutions show that corrections beyond the leading $\mathcal{O}(T^2)$ approximation are particularly relevant for the gauge-boson thermal masses, while they induce a comparatively small shift in the scalar spectrum for the benchmark studied. The self-consistent gauge-boson dressing in the longitudinal sector reduces the barrier in the finite-temperature Higgs effective potential. Implementing the resummation in the transverse sector removes the barrier and would seem to exclude a first-order phase transition in accordance with lattice results. While such resummation is not quantitatively reliable, due to the transverse excitations becoming strongly coupled, the results showcase the crucial role played by transverse modes in determining the nature of the electroweak phase transition.

title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter
abstract: Studying the implications of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on astrophysical objects often requires simulations. N-body simulations are a standard tool but face a few challenges. One is resolving the mean free path in gravothermally collapsing halos. This is necessary to obtain accurate results and is achieved in state-of-the-art simulations by increasing the number of resolution elements. I aim to formulate a numerical scheme that gives an enhanced spatial resolution compared to those methods and allows increasing the resolution without changing the number of resolution elements. The novel scheme that I present is formulated by discarding the classic approach of using kernel functions and computing interaction probabilities. Instead, pairs of particles always interact if their distance is below a specific threshold. Importantly, this distance threshold depends on their relative velocity and the size of the time step. This new formulation no longer requires some of the computations in state-of-the-art schemes and thus helps to increase the performance. Through a variety of test problems with known solutions, I study the accuracy of the new scheme and demonstrate its advantages over state-of-the-art SIDM formulations. Notably, the scheme reduced the computational costs, making the SIDM computations typically much cheaper than gravity. As a consequence, a typical SIDM simulation of isotropic scattering requires only a few percent of its total computational cost for the self-interactions. In conclusion, the new scheme presents an improvement over previous schemes and helps to address current challenges. Besides the enhanced performance, it allows us to achieve a higher accuracy when simulating gravothermally collapsing SIDM halos.

title: Dark vector meson effects on composite dark matter
abstract: We extend previous studies of $\mathcal{G}$-parity-odd dark pion dark matter in a QCD-like $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$ gauge theory with electroweakly interacting dark quarks to include the effects of $\rho$ mesons. We show that vector mesons can substantially affect relic abundance calculations through resonant enhancement, significantly affecting the conditions required to reproduce the observed relic abundance. Electroweak interactions further induce mixing between the dark $\rho$ mesons and Standard Model gauge bosons, opening new decay channels for the dark $\rho$ and modifying the effective interactions of the dark pions. We recast existing ATLAS and CMS searches to constrain the model, and perform a collider phenomenology study targeting the future FCC-hh and muon colliders, focusing on the resonant enhancement of cross sections in the $e^+e^-$, $\mu^+\mu^-$, and $W^+W^-$ final states for the latter. We show that the FCC-hh could probe $\rho$ mesons whose mass is up to 40 TeV.

title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
abstract: The coming years will see what could be the final push in the search for WIMP dark matter (DM), with direct detection reaching into the neutrino fog and indirect detection reaching TeV-scale thermal relics. We study a class of models that these experiments could discover: DM emerging from a warped extra dimension. In the IR, these scenarios appear generically as a $Z'$-type portal. We show that DM with electroweak couplings and TeV scale masses remains viable and discoverable within such a bottom-up context. However, the models require a 20\% tuning between the DM and $Z'$ masses, a tuning that is relaxed if the DM and $Z'$ are strongly coupled and heavier ($\sim$$10$ TeV). In fact, it is the strongly-coupled $Z'$-type portal which is UV-completed by the framework of a warped extra-dimensional Grand Unified Theory (GUT), where DM stability is a spin-off of suppressing proton decay, resulting in a $\sim$$10$ TeV Kaluza-Klein (KK) scale. We identify a variant of this framework where all gauge fields except a baryon-number gauge boson have suppressed couplings to the DM; this model significantly suppresses the direct detection rate, but it remains discoverable through indirect detection. Further, to address the little hierarchy problem associated with $\sim$$10$ TeV KK scale, inspired by the Super-Composite Higgs, we augment our extra-dimensional GUT setup with supersymmetry. We show that this model also possesses a DM candidate, now with a weakly-coupled and $\sim$${\rm TeV}$ mass $Z'$ mediator. In all cases, a near-term discovery remains possible, for instance with the now online Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), suggesting that our first hint of extra dimensions could emerge from the high-energy sky.

title: Casimir Experiments as Spin-Force Detectors
abstract: Precision Casimir experiments enable highly sensitive probes of short range forces, but have thus far constrained only spin-independent interactions. We show that measurements between reversed polarizations of a magnetically compensated source enable direct searches of axion-mediated monopole-dipole forces. The spin force reverses sign, while the common Casimir, gravitational and electrostatic backgrounds broadly cancel. Compensated sources need no intervening shielding, allowing large probes at micrometer gaps. Casimir experiments could probe the couplings $g_p^e g_s^{N}$ and $g_p^e g_s^{e}$ at $\lambda\sim1-100~\mu{\rm m}$ orders of magnitude beyond existing laboratory searches.

title: Charge-resolved four-lepton probes of an $e\mu$-flavour-violating scalar at FCC-ee
abstract: We study a real neutral scalar $X$ with a single flavour-off-diagonal coupling $h_{e\mu}=h_{\mu e}\equiv h$. The coupling induces associated production, $e^+e^-\to e^\pm\mu^\mp X$, and the decay $X\to e^\pm\mu^\mp$. The resulting four-lepton final state separates into the charge-balanced channel $e^+e^-\mu^+\mu^-$ and the same-sign same-flavour channels $e^\pm e^\pm\mu^\mp\mu^\mp$. The charge-balanced channel receives a large prompt continuum background, while the same-sign category has a small estimated background under our benchmark assumptions. We analyse the two channels at FCC-ee for $\sqrt{s}=240~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $\mathcal{L}=10.8~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, including a detector simulation. The collider sensitivities are compared with the one-coupling constraints from the electron and muon magnetic moments, muonium--antimuonium conversion, and LEP dilepton data. At $m_X=146~\mathrm{GeV}$, motivated by the largest excess in the CMS $e\mu$ resonance search, the expected 95\% CL reach of the charge-balanced channel, including a 1\% background uncertainty, is $|h|\simeq 1.0 \times 10^{-2}$, while the same-sign channel reaches $|h|\simeq 1.7 \times 10^{-3}$, compared with the cesium-based electron-$g-2$ bound $|h|<1.46\times10^{-2}$. Both channels thus probe couplings below the present bound. The two signal rates are equal before selection; the difference in reach follows from the different backgrounds.

title: When heavy vectors meet top partners: HVTP, a unified framework for composite Higgs searches
abstract: Vector resonances and top partners are characteristic new states of composite Higgs models: they belong to the same strongly coupled sector, and partial compositeness ties their interactions to the mixings that generate the top mass. Experimental searches, however, usually treat them separately. We provide a common framework for both and release HVTP (Heavy Vectors and Top Partners), a public UFO model for MadGraph in which an electroweak triplet, a hypercharge vector and a colour octet couple to a custodial top-partner multiplet, with all couplings obtained from the exact diagonalisation of the mass matrices. The models and the inputs of our results are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24345218. We translate the latest LHC searches at 13 and 13.6 TeV into the parameter space of the model. In natural scenarios the top partners, which are directly tied to the Higgs mass and to the residual tuning, are lighter than the vector resonances; the vectors then decay mostly into partners and become broad: the standard searches lose much of their sensitivity, while the vectors produce partner pairs at rates that can exceed QCD production. For example, at our benchmark points, with partners near their present limits and an electroweak triplet at about 4 TeV, 73-83% of the triplet decays contain partners, and vector-mediated production reaches up to three times the QCD rate. At the HL-LHC this region can be probed by resonance searches extended to large widths and by partner-pair searches that include resonant production; the latter also reveal the partner spectrum. Composite Higgs models with a non-minimal coset generally also contain a pseudoscalar, which can alter the standard decays of the top partners; we include it in the extension HVTP_eta.

title: Nuclear deep-inelastic scattering as a BSM probe via SMEFT
abstract: Searches for New Physics at the energy frontier have motivated theoretical development of model-independent methods to constrain interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) like the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), as well as associated phenomenological analyses. While these approaches are powerful, they are also afflicted by the large space of higher-dimensional operators and the challenge of possible degeneracies among these operators. To help ameliorate these difficulties, processes beyond those at hadron colliders, including deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), have been identified and studied for their ability to contribute added constraining power. In this work, we extend such investigations to charged-lepton DIS involving heavy nuclei, for which we explore the systematics of SMEFT effects for a series of representative cases. In particular, we point out that nuclear effects can reshuffle the luminosities governing partons entering SMEFT-corrected hard interactions, such that the nucleus can serve as an expanded laboratory to explore SMEFT effects complementary to free-nucleon DIS. In particular, we find that nuclear DIS possesses significant constraining power over flavor-isovector SMEFT operator combinations, with reduced nPDF dependence; similarly, improved control over nPDFs would further enhance the SMEFT reach of nuclear DIS observables. We explore projections for future (proposed) facilities like the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh, finding that improvements to nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) can further sharpen the reach of nuclear DIS.

title: OmniX: A first jet and event model
abstract: Foundation models are a new approach to building machine learning algorithms for particle physics. Their central idea is that a single model can be adapted to a variety of downstream tasks, amortizing training costs. So far, most foundation model prototypes have operated on the constituents of a single jet. This limits their usefulness for physics problems at the scale of full events, such as distinguishing different processes, and restricts their performance, as global correla- tions are invisible to the model. Here, we introduce OmniX, an architecture that operates on both single jets and whole events within a single model. Using the jet-level JetClass and Top-tagging datasets and the event-level Collide-2V dataset, we demonstrate that OmniX trained jointly on single jets and full events matches or exceeds otherwise equivalent jet-only and event-only models in generation and classification.

title: Exotic Portals for Hadronic Processes: The Gluon-Gluon and Gluon-Quark Portals
abstract: In this work we explore all possible light exotic (LEX) particles which are accessible through the gluon-gluon ($g$-$g$) and gluon-quark ($g$-$q$) phenomenological portals up to effective dimension six. We present effective models for these new states, which are directly accessible through gluon and quark fusion processes, and which are guaranteed decays involving Standard Model (SM) quarks and gluons. We note many accessible states in particularly unusual SU(3)$_\text{c}$ representations, which contain large Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. We also include some interesting dimension seven operators with highly unusual features. We also consider all potential spin values for our LEX states, looking at Lorentz representations and color selection rules. In this, we find that states in various unusual Lorentz representations are accessible. We also find that certain operator types have restrictions on allowed color representations based on spin.

title: Quarkonium Energy Correlators in Proton-Proton Collisions: Analytic Calculation and Angular-Momentum Hierarchy
abstract: We present the first complete leading-order (LO) analytic calculation of the quarkonium energy correlator (QEC) in $pp$ collisions, for the color-singlet ${}^3S_1^{[1]}$ and the color-octet ${}^1S_0^{[8]}$, ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$, and ${}^3P_J^{[8]}$ channels of $J/\psi$ production. Instead of the high-$p_T$ fragmentation approximation, the calculation retains the full kinematics of the recoil parton, inverts the map from transverse momentum to the rest-frame angle in closed form, and is validated by \textsc{HELAC-onia} in shape and absolute normalization. We also give the analytic counterpart of the $p_T$-weighted variant of the correlator. The LO shape of each channel is organized by the total angular momentum $J$ of the $c\bar c$ pair, as a consequence of the tree-level selection rule that forbids two on-shell gluons from forming a $J=1$ state. This hierarchy is compressed in the central sPHENIX acceptance and exposed by the wider forward coverage at the LHC. In the distribution normalized to the total cross section, much though not all of the scale uncertainty cancels, leaving promising distinctions in the QEC shapes between different $J/\psi$ production channels. The discriminating power of the QEC can be further improved by next-to-leading-order calculations and by utilizing QECs in simultaneous fits with the $p_T$ spectrum and polarization measurements.

title: Gluon GPDs from hard-exclusive electroproduction of heavy quarkonium at NLO
abstract: Gluon tomography of the nucleon through hard-exclusive electroproduction of $J/\psi$ has been one of the key motivations for Electron-Ion Collider. However, the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations available in the literature were performed either in the collinear factorization limit where the heavy-quark mass is neglected, or in heavy-quark limit where the heavy quarkonia are approximately point-like. We present a full next-to-leading order collinear factorization for the hard exclusive production of heavy mesons that retains the meson mass as well as full light-cone distribution amplitude. We compare the full NLO result with the special limits and estimate the errors due to potentially-large corrections from $\alpha_s(M)$ and $M^2/Q^2$ at this order.

title: Dijet photoproduction in ep and eA collision in POWHEG
abstract: We present the implementation of dijet photoproduction in electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions in the POWHEG BOX V2 Monte Carlo event generator. The process is computed at next-to-leading order in QCD including both direct and resolved photon contributions and is consistently matched to parton showers using the POWHEG method. The implementation is validated by using POWHEG BOX V2 internal consistency checks as well as by comparing fixed-order results with SHERPA. We compare our predictions to dijet photoproduction data from DESY HERA I and II, finding good agreement within theoretical uncertainties, and provide predictions for both electron-proton and electron-gold collisions at the upcoming BNL EIC, illustrating its potential to further constrain both photon and nuclear parton distribution functions.

title: All the Positive Energy Correlators
abstract: We develop a framework to systematically obtain the full set of positivity bounds on multi-point energy correlators for sources of arbitrary spin. The constraints are organized in a family of positive operators $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, with $k=0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. Our approach provides outer bounds, which exclude correlators that violate the positivity of $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, and inner bounds, obtained by constructing ensembles of consistent collider events via linear programming. Both methods converge to each other as numerical precision increases. This approach, in particular, characterizes the allowed higher-point correlators once lower-point correlators are determined. We illustrate this through several examples, including bounds on multipoles of the three-point energy correlator in QCD derived from measurements of one- and two-point correlators at LEP.

title: CEDVR: A virtual reality event display for CMS
abstract: Collision event displays are widely used in high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, enabling researchers to visualize and debug raw and reconstructed event data, and to communicate aspects of individual events to broader audiences. Such event displays are typically viewed on a conventional two-dimensional computer screen. To enhance immersion and interactivity with CMS data, we have developed a virtual reality (VR) software package named CEDVR (for CMS Event Display in Virtual Reality) that uses widely-available VR headsets and hand controllers. This application provides an immersive detector-coordinate view and a novel, complementary LEGO-style view. CEDVR provides easy access to physics object properties and object filtering, and incorporates novel VR features for navigation and object selection. Compatible with consumer-grade Quest headsets, CEDVR is a useful visualization tool for CMS physicists, and contains built-in sample events that support educational and public outreach initiatives.

title: Thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation with the Standard Model
abstract: In warm inflation with the Standard Model (SM), an axion-like inflaton dissipates energy into the plasma through QCD sphaleron transitions. Current predictions assume a friction linear in the bias, defined as the free energy released per transition in units of the temperature. The friction, however, has only been simulated at moderate biases in pure SU(2) gauge theory. We show that, during slow roll, energy conservation, the axial anomaly and thermodynamics relate the bias to the quark chemical potentials generated by the transitions, independently of the form of the friction and of the reaction network in the plasma. A bias within the simulated range requires chemical potentials a few times the temperature, which typically lead to Higgs condensation. Conversely, small chemical potentials imply a large bias and, unless the dissipation is very weak, a temperature far above the axion decay constant, which requires a cutoff of the effective description above that temperature. We illustrate that deviations from linearity beyond the simulated range can change the inflationary dynamics qualitatively, so that reliable predictions require a real-time computation of the friction and the noise in QCD at large bias. With high-scale lepton-number violation, the quark chemical potentials also source a $B-L$ asymmetry that exceeds the observed value by many orders of magnitude already during inflation. Finally, we show that the same relation between the bias and the chemical potentials holds for derivative couplings of the inflaton to SM currents. Unless the dissipation is very weak, warm inflation driven by such couplings therefore requires either a temperature far above the decay constant or chemical potentials that typically lead to Higgs condensation.

title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.

title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
abstract:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2 eta$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $\alpha$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2 eta$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2
u}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2 eta$ decay.

title: Updated T2K measurement of neutrino oscillation parameters with the first data from the Gadolinium-loaded far detector
abstract: The T2K experiment presents updated measurements of neutrino oscillation parameters using $21.4(16.3)\times10^{20}$ protons on target (POT) in (anti-)neutrino mode at the far detector, Super-Kamiokande. This analysis uses an additional neutrino dataset of $1.7 \times 10^{20}$ POT compared to the previous result, and for the very first time, data collected with Super-Kamiokande doped with Gadolinium (Gd). Significant improvements were introduced in the far detector selection and systematic error treatment. Both semi-frequentist and Bayesian analyses are presented, including results on $\sin^{2} \theta_{23}$, $\Delta m^2_{32} $, $\sin^{2} \theta_{13}$ and $\delta_{CP}$. Both analyses favor normal mass ordering with a nearly maximal CP-violating phase and are compatible with neutrino maximal mixing, slightly favouring the upper $\theta_{23}$ octant.

title: Studies of dual ions arriving time reconstruction in N$\nu$DEx time projection chamber
abstract: The N$\nu$DEx experiment aims to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of \(^{82}\)Se with a high-pressure \(^{82}\)SeF\(_6\) negative-ion time projection chamber. In the assumed two-carrier model, the arrival-time separation of SeF\(_5^-\) and SeF\(_6^-\) can estimate the longitudinal coordinate without an external trigger. We compare FFT deconvolution and direct waveform fitting on simulated Topmetal-S charge-sensitive-amplifier waveforms. With the fixed amplifier response, direct fitting and FFT accepted 873 and 855 of 873 geometry-selected single depositions, respectively. On the 855 common events, the arrival-time separation RMSEs were 0.180 and 0.222 ms. Numerical depth calibration gave mean \(z\) residuals of 0.036 and 0.075 cm and RMSEs of 0.192 and 0.208 cm on 848 common events. With sampled CSA shaping, FFT accepted the same 855 waveforms and direct fitting accepted 866 of 873. On the four-way common sample of 855 events, the direct-fit separation RMSE was 0.180~ms with fixed shaping and 0.217~ms with sampled shaping. An accepted near-readout direct fit outside the FFT sample had a 184~ms separation error, giving an RMSE of 6.25~ms over all accepted sampled-response direct fits. With the fixed response, the full-track fit retained 1,185 of 1,810 observed pads in 100 selected Geant4 events. The median event-level depth RMSE was 0.184 cm. Subtracting each event's mean Monte Carlo residual gave a median event-centred RMS of 0.102 cm as a diagnostic of relative track shape. The absolute depth remains sensitive to the common event time. Validation with detector data is needed to assess the effects of diffusion, electronics noise, and inter-pad response.

title: Measurements of $|V_{cd(s)}|$ , decay constants, and form factors in (semi-)leptonic $D_{(s)}$ decays at BESIII
abstract: The BESIII experiment accumulated the world's largest charm-meson samples. This proceeding presents recent measurements of decay constants, transition form factors, and CKM matrix elements from (semi-)leptonic \(D^+\) and \(D_s^+\) decays based on these datasets.

title: On the effective atmospheric-scale $\Delta m^2$ in neutrino oscillation
abstract: We discuss an effective two-frequency description of the three-generation neutrino oscillation with the key quantity $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$, which unifies the effects of atmospheric-scale $\Delta m^2_{31}$-$\Delta m^2_{32}$ driven oscillations. As a solution to the minimization problem in vacuum, Nunokawa {\it et al.} obtained $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} } = \Delta m^2_{31} - (2E / L) \arctan \left\{ r_{2} \sin 2\Delta_{21} / ( r_{1} + r_{2} \cos 2\Delta_{21} ) \right\}$, where $\Delta_{21} \equiv \Delta m^2_{21} L / (4 E)$ and $r_{i}$ are the mixing-angle dependent constants. Despite the skepticism for the $L/E$ dependence in this formula, we show, in fact, that this is an exact expression, which renders the probability formula also exact. We offer an appealing-to-intuition physical explanation for the $L/E$ dependence that it originates from the nature-designed three generation neutrinos. The way it is buried into $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ is through the solar-effect renormalization to this quantity. With the physical interpretation of $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ at hand, we aim at resolving the existing controversies on $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ in this paper.

title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
abstract: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $\lambda_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

title: Description of the decay $\phi \to \pi^+\pi^-$ in the NJL chiral quark model
abstract: The doubly suppressed decay $\phi \to \pi^+\pi^-$ is described in the chiral NJL quark model. This decay occurs in violation of the OZI rule and isotopic invariance. Two possible channels are considered. The first channel involves $\phi-\omega$ mixing and the subsequent decay of $\omega \to \pi^+\pi^-$. In the second channel, the decay occurs via an intermediate $\rho$ meson.

title: Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals from Higher Residue Pairings
abstract: We develop a method for constructing differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from multivariate intersection numbers, without fibration. The large-$\varepsilon$ expansion of the intersection pairing, with $\varepsilon$ the dimensional regulator, is given by Saito's higher residue pairings, which localise at the critical points of a potential and admit closed multivariate formulae. In the Lee-Pomeransky representation, applying these formulae to Feynman integrals requires analytic regulators $\delta$ on the coordinate hyperplanes, and the physical limit $\delta \to 0$ is not manifest. Assuming that the regulated critical points are analytic in $\delta$, we show that, as $\delta \to 0$, they organise into sectors labelled by sets of pinched propagators. We derive closed formulae for the leading and first subleading higher residue pairings in this limit, written entirely in terms of unregulated sector data. These suffice to reconstruct differential systems at most linear in $\varepsilon$, including canonical ones, bypassing integration-by-parts identities. We apply the method to the massless planar four-point ladder families up to four loops and obtain their canonical differential equations, which are new at four loops.

title: Two-loop QCD amplitudes for $pp\to\gamma\gamma$ with a top-quark loop
abstract: We revisit the computation of two-loop QCD amplitudes for diphoton production in the quark- and gluon-initiated channels, focusing on contributions involving a closed top-quark loop. We derive analytic expressions for the finite remainders in terms of a set of special functions constructed from the $\epsilon$-expanded components of master integrals. We employ a canonical basis of master integrals for the polylogarithmic sectors, while retaining a noncanonical basis for the elliptic sectors. The analytic cancellation of ultraviolet and infrared poles is established by deriving relations among master integral components. Relations among polylogarithmic components are derived numerically from their differential equations and we utilise a set of finite Feynman integrals, constructed using local numerator insertions and constraints from soft and collinear limits, to derive relations between pole-contributing elliptic master integral components and the polylogarithmic ones. The construction does not rely on a particular choice of noncanonical elliptic master integral basis. The resulting set of special functions is minimal in the polylogarithmic sectors, whereas the elliptic components contributing to the finite part of the amplitudes are potentially overcomplete. The special functions are evaluated numerically by solving systems of differential equations, enabling their computation across the physical phase space. We present a C++ implementation of the corresponding hard functions, suitable for on-the-fly numerical evaluation in cross-section calculations.

title: Azimuthal Correlations of Heavy-Quark Pairs in Ultraperipheral Collisions
abstract: We study azimuthal correlations of $D\bar D$ and $B\bar B$ pairs in Xn0n-selected Pb--Pb ultraperipheral collisions at $\sqrt{s}=5.36~\mathrm{TeV}$. The selection requires neutron emission from the target nucleus and no neutron emission from the photon source. The unpolarized and linearly polarized Weizs\"acker--Williams gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distributions are modeled in the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework and evolved to the hard scale. We keep the full mass dependence of the Born coefficients and the one-gluon soft current. The photon flux includes the neutron selection and is averaged over the target area. We present the transverse-momentum and rapidity dependence of the $\cos(2\phi_h)$ and $\cos(4\phi_h)$ asymmetries. Over the ranges studied, both moments increase with the pair total transverse momentum and decrease with its relative transverse momentum. For the lowest relative transverse momentum interval considered, the $D\bar D$ moments are larger than those for $B\bar B$. In the kinematic region considered, the $\cos(2\phi_h)$ asymmetry is much larger than the $\cos(4\phi_h)$ asymmetry, and the contribution from gluon linear polarization is small compared with the total angular modulation.

title: The impact of phase transitions on dilepton production
abstract: We calculate dielectron yields at beam energies relevant for the CBM experiment at FAIR and the STAR Beam Energy Scan. The production of intermediate mass dielectrons is expected to increase in presence of a phase transition due to the latent heat. In this work, we use the SMASH+vHLLE hybrid model to quantify this enhancement in two scenarios: with a toy equation of state consisting of the Bag Model and Hadron Resonance Gas, separated by a Maxwell-constructed transition; and with a more realistic equation of state containing a critical endpoint, based on the 3D Ising universality class. We confirm that the dilepton yield increases when the system passes through a first-order phase transition, by about 7% in the realistic scenario.

title: Parton Branching evolution in updfevolv: NNLO spacelike evolution in the ZM-VFNS and NLO timelike evolution with heavy-flavour matching
abstract: We describe two extensions of the Parton Branching (PB) method as implemented in updfevolv: the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) spacelike DGLAP evolution of parton densities in the zero-mass variable-flavour-number scheme (ZM-VFNS), and the leading and next-to-leading order (LO, NLO) timelike evolution of fragmentation functions, including the heavy-flavour matching conditions at the quark thresholds. We summarise the timelike PB formalism - momentum sum rule, Sudakov form factor, branching chain and kinematics. We give implementation details needed for the PB formalism to reproduce the semi-analytical solutions of APFEL for all flavours, including heavy quarks at threshold. This note supplements the updfevolv manual and is a technical release note for updfevolv version 2.6.0.

title: A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal
abstract: We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a St\"uckelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and St\"uckelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling. We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_\chi\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{\chi,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.

title: Multiscale Zoom-in Lattice Simulation for Inflation
abstract: Lattice simulations are a powerful tool for studying the nonlinear evolution of inflationary fluctuations. The exponential expansion, however, makes it challenging to cover a broad range of scales relevant for the dynamics, limiting how many e-folds a single fixed grid can follow. We develop a three-dimensional zoom-in lattice method to follow inflationary fluctuations over a broad range of scales from the adiabatic subhorizon regime through horizon crossing. Every few e-folds, the grid is refined into one or more subgrids, with small-scale power injected and large-scale fluctuations inherited from previous generations. Each zoom shifts the resolved band while keeping its dynamic range fixed. This extends the duration over which lattice simulations can follow inflationary fluctuations from a few e-folds to tens of e-folds. In a Starobinsky benchmark evolved for 50 e-folds, the curvature power spectrum agrees with linear theory. In a model with an oscillatory feature, the zoom-in simulations recover the peak seen in a high-resolution fixed-grid run and show scale-dependent non-Gaussianity.

title: Perturbative unitarity bounds from qubit entanglement in scalar scattering and QED
abstract: In the framework of $2\to 2$ relativistic scattering described by the perturbative $S$-matrix, we perform a comprehensive analysis of the properties of quantum channels obtained by tracing out the momentum from the scattered state. We work in two distinct scenarios with qubit degrees of freedom: flavored scalar contact interactions and QED, focusing in particular on initial-state leptons with transverse polarization. We identify the conditions that make the quantum channel unitary, calculate the entanglement of the qubits through the concurrence, and use its maximally allowed value to extract perturbativity upper bounds on the coupling constants. We find that the limits are often more constraining than the corresponding partial-wave expansion bounds, and that they allow us to bypass some of the obstacles associated in the latter with the singular behavior of forward scattering.

title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
abstract: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

title: The Four-Loop Ladder Integral Family for the QED Electron Self-Energy
abstract: We compute the complete set of master integrals of the four-loop ladder integral family contributing to the electron self-energy in Quantum Electrodynamics. We obtain the results through canonical differential equations and write them as iterated integrals over integration kernels related to different parametrizations of the sunrise elliptic curve and a Calabi-Yau threefold. The rich structure of geometries and couplings between them requires the introduction of a large number of extra transcendental functions to reach $\epsilon$-factorization. We discuss explicitly how to find a canonical basis for a selection of particularly interesting sectors. Additionally, we compute local series expansions and numerical boundary constants at $p^2=\infty$ and $p^2=m^2$ up to weight seven, and for the polylogarithmic constants we find analytical representations by numerical matching. The on-shell boundary values of this single family already span all non-polylogarithmic constants entering the planar contribution to the four-loop result for the anomalous magnetic moment $(g-2)$ of the electron. We obtain precise numerical results across all values of $p^2$ using numerical transport.

title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
abstract: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

title: Dark Matter Assisted Axion-Magnetic Resonance
abstract: An oscillating axion dark matter (DM) background can enhance the conversion of another relativistic axion into photons when traversing a magnetic field. The DM background rotates photon polarization relative the magnetic orientation, which compensates the photon's and the propagating axion's dispersion relation mismatch. We relate this mechanism to Axion Magnetic Resonance (AMR) and apply it to stellar axions in the starburst galaxy M82. We analyze its enhancement to the resulting X-ray signals while accounting for the finite magnetic domain size, dark matter coherence length, DM density morphology, plasma profiles, and the detector response. We derive strong constraints using existing X-ray data from NuSTAR. We show that this resonant conversion can lead to $\mathcal O(10^2)$ enhancement in the photon-axion conversion probability, improving the upper limits on axion's photon coupling over part of the mass range where ordinary conversion is suppressed. We also show that this type of resonance predicts distinctive features in the hard X-ray spectrum, which is moderately favored by the data over the background only model, yet it is currently still consistent with statistical fluctuations.

title: Multi-Component Axion Dark Matter Revisited and the Role of Ultralight ALPs
abstract: In this work, we revisit the multi-component axion dark matter (DM) scenario and explore the role of ultralight axion-like particles (ALPs). After briefly reviewing maximal axion mixing, we incorporate a stochastic axion mixing mechanism that generalizes it by relaxing the requirement of a uniform hierarchy among the axion decay constants. We find that, depending on the parameters, either the QCD axion or an ALP can dominate the DM abundance after mixing; once axion mass contributions are included, the heaviest ALPs tend to prevail. In a two-component framework, stochastic mixing significantly enlarges the allowed parameter space for the QCD axion decay constant, enabling the QCD axion to constitute the entirety of cold DM. The corresponding ALP mass range remains largely unconstrained by current experiments and is within reach of future searches. In the multi-component case, a larger ALP population leads to the emergence of more ultralight ALPs with large decay constants. These ultralight ALPs represent compelling targets for upcoming axion searches.

title: The relativistic BCS-BEC crossover in closed form: the cutoff as an effective range
abstract: At zero temperature the mean-field potential of a Dirac fermion with a pairing gap contains one momentum integral, that of the sum of its two quasiparticle levels. We evaluate it in closed form from a geometric construction: the two levels are distances in a plane, and the momentum line is a finite arc of a fixed ellipse, along which the charge, the scalar density and the pair amplitude, summed over the modes, are combinations of Legendre's three elliptic integrals. As the upper limit of the momentum grows, the integral grows by a quartic term, a quadratic term and a logarithm with a known coefficient. The two powers are absorbed into a constant and into the coupling, and with all momenta integrated what remains is a finite combination of Legendre's integrals and the logarithm of one scale $\lambda$. The gap equation and the density of the relativistic BCS-BEC crossover follow in closed form. Once the coupling has been traded for the scattering length, $\lambda$ takes the place of the cutoff that the literature keeps as a third parameter. We show that it fixes the effective range of the channel of the pair: for a pair of Dirac fermions of mass $m$ with the pairing vertex $\gamma_5$, $r_e=-(4/\pi m)[\ln(2\lambda/m)-1]$. At low density and a fixed $k_Fr_e$ the crossover is that of the two-channel model of a Feshbach resonance with the same scattering length and effective range. In the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model the pion decay constant fixes $\lambda$, the effective range of the pion channel is $-8\pi f_\pi^{2}/(N_cM^{3})$, and the constituent mass $M$ of the quark is the one parameter that remains free.

title: Z-Boson Production in Proton-Lead Collisions with MRW Nuclear TMDs
abstract: The production of dileptons in proton-lead collisions probes the transverse-momentum structure of partons in a nuclear environment. We summarize a $k_t$-factorization study of $Z$ boson production at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16\,\mathrm{TeV}$, comparing transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions constructed with leading-order and Next-to-leading-order Martin-Ryskin-Watt (LO-MRW and NLO-MRW) prescriptions. Parton-level predictions obtained with \textsc{KaTie} are confronted with the CMS measurements in two invariant-mass regions, using the dilepton transverse momentum, $\phi^*_\eta$ and center-of-mass rapidity. The models describe the overall trends near the $Z$ resonance, while the virtuality constraint in NLO-MRW changes the high-transverse-momentum behavior. At lower dilepton masses, both prescriptions underestimate parts of the data, particularly the NLO-MRW result. These comparisons illustrate both the potential and the limitations of last-step-evolution nuclear TMD models for $Z$ boson production in proton-nucleus collisions.

title: Boosted energy-energy correlators in the small-acoplanarity limit
abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator in the hadronic decay of a boosted boson. We focus on the small-acoplanarity region, where the two hadron momenta are nearly back-to-back in the plane transverse to the boson momentum. We derive a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization formula for electroweak and Higgs bosons in this region, expressed directly in boosted-frame variables in terms of hard, soft, and jet functions with a one-dimensional recoil measurement. We verify its singular real-emission terms at next-to-leading order and present resummed predictions up to N$^3$LL for asymmetric $e^+e^-$ colliders. For vector bosons, the azimuthal orientation of the hadron pair about the boost axis is sensitive to the transverse-spin correlation of the produced quarks through the Collins fragmentation function. We study this sensitivity for photon-tagged $Z$ bosons in $e^+e^-\to Z\gamma$ and compare our predictions with simulations using PYTHIA 8 supplemented by StringSpinner.

title: The Sensitivity of Higgs Factories to the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model via Precision Measurements
abstract: Precision measurements of Higgs boson couplings at future Higgs factories provide an indirect probe of new particles at mass scales beyond the reach of the high luminosity run of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). We study this sensitivity in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), focusing on radiative corrections to the third-generation Yukawa couplings. In particular, supersymmetric threshold corrections to the bottom Yukawa coupling and, in a smaller parameter region, to the tau Yukawa coupling, can remain significant even for multi-TeV superpartner masses. We perform a numerical survey of the MSSM parameter space, using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo, in order to identify models consistent with a 125 GeV Higgs boson and exhibiting potentially observable Higgs-coupling deviations. We find that precision measurements of the bottom Yukawa coupling can probe heavy Higgs masses of order 2-3 TeV and retain sensitivity to gluinos, Higgsinos, and bottom squarks with masses above 5 TeV. The corresponding sensitivity in the {\tau} Yukawa coupling is also present but more limited in parameter space. These results illustrate the characteristic pattern of Higgs-coupling deviations predicted by the MSSM. They demonstrate that precision Higgs measurements can provide sensitivity to supersymmetric physics well beyond the expected direct-search reach of the HL-LHC.

title: CANON: Agent-Assisted Construction of Canonical Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals
abstract: The construction of canonical basis is an important procedure in the calculation of multi-loop Feynman integrals via the canonical differential equation methods. Currently, there are various different methods for this purpose. Among them, no single method is universally applicable. Thus, obtaining a valid basis often requires repeated attempts and verification. In this paper, we present CANON, an agent-assisted framework designed to make this search-and-verification process more convenient and more efficient. In this workflow, the agent selects methods and calls the corresponding tools to revise the basis proposal or the associated differential-equation system. Independent programs then verify whether the agent's result is valid and ask the agent to retry if verification fails. This framework contains a specific state-management tool to supports long-range basis searching works which requires multiple sub-agents. Its modular architecture enables future extensions to the framework itself. In this paper, we demonstrate this framework by applying it to some two-loop and three-loop integral families.

title: Triple-Higgs production: a window on the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings
abstract: We present a comprehensive study of triple-Higgs production within the $\kappa$-framework as a probe of the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings. At leading order, we derive compact parametrisations of the inclusive $gg\to3h$ cross section in terms of the trilinear and quartic Higgs self-coupling modifiers $\kappa_3$ and $\kappa_4$, the top-quark Yukawa coupling modifier $\kappa_t$, and the anomalous two-top-two-Higgs and two-top-three-Higgs coupling modifiers $\kappa_{2t}$ and $\kappa_{3t}$. These parametrisations allow for a fast and accurate interpretation of current and future LHC measurements. Applying them to LHC Run 2 data and high-luminosity LHC projections, we quantify the impact of $\kappa_t$, $\kappa_{2t}$, and $\kappa_{3t}$ on the constraints on $\kappa_3$ and $\kappa_4$, and derive the first direct constraint on $\kappa_{3t}$ from existing LHC data. We further show that parameter points yielding nearly identical inclusive rates can give rise to different kinematic distributions, demonstrating the potential of differential measurements to resolve degeneracies and enhance the sensitivity of future triple-Higgs searches.

title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.
